questions.question_text:
The vectors $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}x\\-5\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}$ satisfy $\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}=1$.
Find the value of $x$.

options.why: Solved $4x=-16$ instead of $4x=16$ after moving the $-15$ across.
Stopped at $4x=16$ without dividing by $4$.
Took $(-4)\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)$ as $+5$, giving $-9+5$.
Used only the first product $\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)(-6)$ and omitted the second product.
Multiplied across the pair, $\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)+(-4)(-6)$, giving $\frac{15}{8}+24$.

Find $\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}$.

questions.question_text:
The vectors $\begin{pmatrix}x\\-\frac{5}{2}\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{3}{4}\\\frac{8}{5}\end{pmatrix}$ have a dot product of $\frac{7}{2}$.
Find the value of $x$.

options.why: Took the second product as $+4$, solving $-\frac{3}{4}x+4=\frac{7}{2}$.
Ignored the negative in the first component of the second vector, solving $\frac{3}{4}x-4=\frac{7}{2}$.
Stopped at $-\frac{3}{4}x=\frac{15}{2}$ without dividing by $-\frac{3}{4}$.
